title: Cell types
examples: What is the main difference between a plant cell and an animal cell?
Can you explain what makes a cell prokaryotic?
Do all living things have eukaryotic cells?

explain.say: Today we will look at different kinds of cells you might find. We will learn about their basic differences.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: an animal cell. Look at the cell membrane, the cytoplasm and the nucleus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Some cells are very simple and do not have a nucleus. These are called prokaryotic cells. Bacteria are a common example of this type of cell.
Other cells are much more complex and have a true nucleus. These are called eukaryotic cells. Most animals and plants have this type of cell.
Plant cells have a rigid outer layer called a cell wall. Animal cells do not have this strong outer wall structure.

draw.text: Plant cell wall vs Animal cell

explain.say: Plant cells also usually have chloroplasts for making food. Animal cells get energy from eating other things.

faq.q: What is the main difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
faq.a: The main difference is the nucleus. Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus, while prokaryotic cells do not.
asks: How do I tell if a cell is prokaryotic?
Does a nucleus mean a cell is complex?

faq.q: Do all plant cells have a cell wall?
faq.a: Yes, most plant cells have a cell wall outside their cell membrane. This gives them a fixed, rigid shape.
asks: What is the purpose of the cell wall?
Can plant cells live without a cell wall?

faq.a: Yes, animal cells are always eukaryotic. They have all the complex parts like a nucleus.
asks: What kind of cells are animals made of?

faq.q: What is the function of the chloroplast in a plant cell?
faq.a: Chloroplasts are where photosynthesis happens. They use sunlight to make food for the plant to live on.
asks: How do plants make their own food?
Where does the energy for a plant come from?

faq.q: Can a cell have both a cell wall and chloroplasts?
faq.a: Yes, plant cells typically have both a cell wall and chloroplasts. These are key features of plant life.
asks: Are these features exclusive to plants?

facts: Prokaryotic cells lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
Eukaryotic cells contain a defined nucleus that holds the cell's DNA.
Plant cells are characterized by having a cell wall outside the membrane.
Chloroplasts are organelles found in plant cells used for photosynthesis.

quiz.say: Which cell type has a true nucleus surrounding its DNA?
quiz.why: Eukaryotic cells are defined by having a true, membrane-bound nucleus to keep their genetic material safe.

wrong.0: Animal cells are eukaryotic, but 'Eukaryotic' is the broader, correct classification answer.
wrong.2: Prokaryotic cells are specifically known for lacking a true nucleus.
wrong.3: Plant is a type, not the general cell structure feature being tested.

quiz.say: A cell that makes its own food using sunlight must have which structure?
quiz.why: Chloroplasts are the specific organelles responsible for capturing light energy and making food through photosynthesis.

wrong.0: The cell wall provides structure but does not make food.
wrong.1: Mitochondria release energy from food, they do not capture light.
wrong.2: The nucleus controls the cell but does not perform photosynthesis.

quiz.say: Which cell type is most likely to have both a cell wall and chloroplasts?
quiz.why: Plant cells are the classic example of eukaryotic cells possessing both a rigid cell wall and chloroplasts.

wrong.0: Animal cells lack a cell wall and chloroplasts.
wrong.1: Bacteria cells are prokaryotic and lack chloroplasts.
wrong.2: Yeast cells are fungi and typically lack chloroplasts.
